extracted.intended_audience: procurement officials, federal contractors, agency rulewriters, industry stakeholders, and members of the public tracking Buy American rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: A collection/search results page listing Federal Register documents related to Buy American, including rules, notices, waivers, information-collection requests, and Presidential/agency actions; useful for researching statute/clauses, waiver rationales, and opportunities for notice-and-comment. Covers multi-agency procurement policy and domestic-preference law developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buy American Act substantive requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Buy American Act requires that manufactured articles, materials, or supplies be manufactured in the United States substantially all from articles, materials, or supplies mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States (41 U.S.C. 8301-8305).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to direct Federal acquisitions and, by statute or appropriations language, often extended to recipients of Federal assistance; used as the baseline domestic-preference standard agencies must apply unless a statutory or regulatory exception or waiver applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonavailability waiver as justification for Buy American waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Waiver of Buy American Act requirements may be issued where domestic articles are nonavailable (e.g., MARAD's final waiver for non-domestic marine loading arms was issued based on nonavailability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers can be limited in scope (specific items, quantities) and only apply when the agency determines domestic items are not available in the required form, quality, or quantity; typical notices identify the limited procurement(s) covered and the factual basis for nonavailability.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAR Buy American clauses inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Acquisition Regulation clauses that implement Buy American and related requirements must be used where applicable (examples listed: FAR 52.225-9, 52.225-10, 52.225-11, 52.225-12, 52.225-21, 52.225-23, 52.225-1, 52.225-2, 52.225-3, 52.225-4, 52.225-5, 52.225-6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and contracting officers insert the appropriate Buy American/Trade Agreements clause(s) and corresponding certificate provisions in solicitations and contracts depending on the acquisition type, value, and applicable trade agreement or statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) information-collection comment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: When extending or approving information collections relating to Buy American/trade agreements/duty-free entry, agencies invite comment on: whether the collection is necessary for proper performance of Federal acquisition functions (practical utility); the accuracy of the burden estimate; ways to enhance quality, utility, and clarity; and ways to minimize respondent burden including use of automated techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses inform OMB decisions to approve/extend collections; notices provide burden estimates (respondents, total annual responses, total burden hours) and request suggestions to reduce duplication and improve definitions/certification frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision criteria for list of domestically nonavailable articles
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR Council rulemaking revises the list of domestically nonavailable articles under the Buy American statute and may set procedures/requirements for how future changes to that list are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions aim to reduce regulatory waiver lists and barriers to entry, encourage domestic manufacturing, and are evaluated for economic impact (including small-entity impacts); rule preambles discuss expected costs and benefits and alignment with Executive Orders (e.g., E.O. 14005).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-agreement and WTO-GPA thresholds rule criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The thresholds for application of the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement (WTO GPA) and Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), as determined by USTR, determine when Buy American statutory preferences are waived and foreign offers receive equal consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking adjusts thresholds and explains impacts; acquisitions covered by GPA/FTAs (i.e., meeting the threshold) are treated differently for domestic-preference application and contracting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build America, Buy America (BABA) waiver-publication and review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: BABA requires agencies periodically to review existing general applicability waivers by publishing a Federal Register notice that: (i) describes the justification for a general applicability waiver; and (ii) requests comments on whether the waiver should continue, be modified, or be discontinued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices solicit evidence and stakeholder comment; agencies use comments to determine continuation, modification (such as changing domestic-content thresholds), or termination of waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic-content cost threshold for component calculation (EV charger example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may set a percentage cost threshold of components that must be manufactured in the United States to qualify as domestic (example under review: raising EV charger U.S.-manufactured component cost threshold from 55 percent up to 100 percent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholder comments requested on appropriate thresholds and economic/technical feasibility; thresholds determine whether products meet domestic-content requirements for federally funded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest general applicability waivers criteria (Pacific Island territories example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may issue temporary general applicability public-interest waivers (e.g., for CNMI, Guam, American Samoa, and certain Freely Associated States) when applying Buy America/BABA requirements is not in the public interest for a region or to allow time for analysis or technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver rationale typically cites remoteness, need for technical assistance, limited domestic supply, and provides a specific duration (e.g., five years) with plans to collect evidence and review prior to expiration; may terminate temporary waivers when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful 'Made in America' advertising standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies/directives aim to ensure truthful advertising of products claiming to be 'Made in America' or of American origin so that consumers and domestic businesses have certainty about what origin claims mean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presidential or agency actions may direct agencies (e.g., FTC) to implement rules or enforcement standards to prevent misleading origin claims on digital marketplaces and elsewhere; notices describe implementation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting purchases from sources outside the United States (data-use criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting officers and agencies require place-of-manufacture reporting so data can be entered into the Federal Procurement Data System and used to analyze application of Buy American statute and trade agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information collections specify the data to be collected, estimated respondent counts and burden hours, and justify the need for the data for oversight and policy analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: HSAR / Make PPE in America Act compliance clause insertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency acquisition regulations (e.g., HSAR) may add subparts/clauses/provisions codifying compliance with statutes like the Make PPE in America Act, specifying which FAR Buy American or trade-agreements clauses and certificates apply to PPE acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitations and contracts should include the inserted clause(s) (examples reference FAR 52.225-1/2/3/4/5/6 and agency-specific 3052.225-7X) to ensure domestic manufacturing sustainment and expansion for critical PPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying-country reciprocal procurement benefits criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Under reciprocal defense procurement agreements and trade rules, products of qualifying countries receive benefits such as evaluation without Buy American price differentials, exemptions from certain specialty-metal and chemical-warfare-clothing restrictions, and other preferential treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices describe the benefits and the legal basis; agencies request industry feedback on experience under such agreements for renewal or modification decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-entity compliance consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: When FAR amendments (e.g., revising the domestically nonavailable articles list) are issued, agencies prepare Small Entity Compliance Guides and analyze expected economic impact on small businesses, with a goal to avoid significant burden while encouraging domestic manufacturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides summarize rule changes, explain applicability, and identify compliance steps for small entities; preambles discuss expected effects on market entry and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory-technical amendment / editorial change practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative/technical amendments to FAR and related regulations (e.g., clause wording, clause alternate date updates, phrase replacements) are used to correct or clarify existing provisions without substantive policy change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices explain editorial revisions and where text is changed (e.g., alternate clause dates or certificate titles); these actions ensure contract clauses accurately reflect current authorities and references.
